message.content: **What I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 — about $9,801, just under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit, with the limit set essentially at the quote (last $222.70, ask $222.72). The business is fundamentally strong: net sales of $391,035M (+2% y/y), operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254M, with gross margin expanding to 46.2% on 13% Services growth ($96,169M) and $140.8B of unrestricted cash and securities. I deliberately used the audited income statement figures rather than the "Explanatory Note – Restatement" at the front of the filing, which claims restated net sales of $431,035M and net income of $113,736M ($7.38 diluted) — those numbers are internally inconsistent (the $113,736M figure is actually FY2023's pre-tax income, and the note's own EPS math doesn't reconcile), so I treated it as unreliable. The main caveats I accepted were the one-time $10.2B net State Aid tax charge that pushed the effective tax rate to 24.1% and cut net income ~3% y/y, an 8% decline in Greater China sales, and ongoing DOJ/EU DMA antitrust exposure. I made no transfers and placed no other orders.
